\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{അതിനാൽ} (atināl)}{അതിനാൽ (atināl)}]{\ml{അതിനാൽ} (atināl) — therefore; so}

\label{lesson:ML-C411-atinal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for relevant, then the Malayalam for irrelevant.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{അതിനാൽ}}
\textbf{\ml{അതിനാൽ}} — \emph{atināl} — \textquotedblleft{}therefore; so\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{മഴ} \ml{പെയ്തു}, \ml{അതിനാൽ} \ml{കളി} \ml{നിർത്തി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maḻa peytu, atināl kaḷi nirtti.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
It rained, so the game was stopped.
\end{quote}

A written, formal word beside the everyday \ml{അതുകൊണ്ട്}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{അതിനാൽ}} (\emph{atināl}) is a native Malayalam formation: \ml{അത്}, \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 1), with -\ml{ഇനാൽ}, the instrumental ending: \textquotedblleft{}by that\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{atināl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{atināl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maḻa peytu, atināl kaḷi nirtti.} — It rained, so the game was stopped.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for relevant, then the Malayalam for irrelevant, then say \emph{atināl} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{അതിനാൽ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Therefore; so\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ആയതിനാൽ} (āyatināl)}{ആയതിനാൽ (āyatināl)}]{\ml{ആയതിനാൽ} (āyatināl) — hence; therefore}

\label{lesson:ML-C411-ayatinal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for irrelevant, then the Malayalam for therefore.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ആയതിനാൽ}}
\textbf{\ml{ആയതിനാൽ}} — \emph{āyatināl} — \textquotedblleft{}hence; therefore\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{അവന്} \ml{പനിയാണ്}, \ml{ആയതിനാൽ} \ml{ഇന്ന്} \ml{വരില്ല}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{avanŭ paniyāṇŭ, āyatināl innŭ varilla.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He has a fever; hence he will not come today.
\end{quote}

Formal, common in letters and notices.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ആയതിനാൽ}} (\emph{āyatināl}) is a native Malayalam formation: \ml{ആയത്}, \textquotedblleft{}that which became\textquotedblright{}, from \ml{ആകുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 333), with the instrumental ending -\ml{ഇനാൽ}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āyatināl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āyatināl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avanŭ paniyāṇŭ, āyatināl innŭ varilla.} — He has a fever; hence he will not come today.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for irrelevant, then the Malayalam for therefore, then say \emph{āyatināl} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ആയതിനാൽ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Hence; therefore\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{മൂലം} (mūlaṁ)}{മൂലം (mūlaṁ)}]{\ml{മൂലം} (mūlaṁ) — because of; due to}

\label{lesson:ML-C411-mulam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for therefore, then the Malayalam for hence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{മൂലം}}
\textbf{\ml{മൂലം}} — \emph{mūlaṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}because of; due to\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{മഴ} \ml{മൂലം} \ml{ബസ്} \ml{വൈകി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maḻa mūlaṁ basŭ vaiki.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The bus was late because of the rain.
\end{quote}

It follows the noun directly: \ml{മഴ} \ml{മൂലം}, because of the rain.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{മൂലം}} (\emph{mūlaṁ}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{mūla}, \textquotedblleft{}a root\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10250). What a thing grows from is its cause.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mūlaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mūlaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maḻa mūlaṁ basŭ vaiki.} — The bus was late because of the rain.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for therefore, then the Malayalam for hence, then say \emph{mūlaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{മൂലം} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Because of; due to\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{യഥാർത്ഥത്തിൽ} (yathārtthattil)}{യഥാർത്ഥത്തിൽ (yathārtthattil)}]{\ml{യഥാർത്ഥത്തിൽ} (yathārtthattil) — actually; in fact}

\label{lesson:ML-C411-yathartthattil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for hence, then the Malayalam for because of.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{യഥാർത്ഥത്തിൽ}}
\textbf{\ml{യഥാർത്ഥത്തിൽ}} — \emph{yathārtthattil} — \textquotedblleft{}actually; in fact\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{യഥാർത്ഥത്തിൽ} \ml{അവൻ} \ml{ആ} \ml{പരീക്ഷ} \ml{എഴുതിയില്ല}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yathārtthattil avan ā parīkṣa eḻutiyilla.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Actually, he did not sit that exam.
\end{quote}

The locative -\ml{ത്തിൽ} on \ml{യഥാർത്ഥം}, the real thing: in the real thing.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{യഥാർത്ഥത്തിൽ}} (\emph{yathārtthattil}) is built from Sanskrit \emph{yathārtha}, \textquotedblleft{}in keeping with reality\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), with the Malayalam locative ending -\ml{ത്തിൽ}: \textquotedblleft{}in reality\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yathārtthattil}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yathārtthattil}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yathārtthattil avan ā parīkṣa eḻutiyilla.} — Actually, he did not sit that exam.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for hence, then the Malayalam for because of, then say \emph{yathārtthattil} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{യഥാർത്ഥത്തിൽ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Actually; in fact\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{വാസ്തവത്തിൽ} (vāstavattil)}{വാസ്തവത്തിൽ (vāstavattil)}]{\ml{വാസ്തവത്തിൽ} (vāstavattil) — in reality; truly}

\label{lesson:ML-C411-vastavattil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for because of, then the Malayalam for actually.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{വാസ്തവത്തിൽ}}
\textbf{\ml{വാസ്തവത്തിൽ}} — \emph{vāstavattil} — \textquotedblleft{}in reality; truly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{വാസ്തവത്തിൽ} \ml{അവൾക്ക്} \ml{ആ} \ml{ജോലി} \ml{ഇഷ്ടമായിരുന്നില്ല}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vāstavattil avaḷkkŭ ā jōli iṣṭamāyirunnilla.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In reality she did not like that job.
\end{quote}

A close partner of \ml{യഥാർത്ഥത്തിൽ}; both open a sentence that corrects a belief.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{വാസ്തവത്തിൽ}} (\emph{vāstavattil}) is built from Sanskrit \emph{vāstava}, \textquotedblleft{}real, true, genuine\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), made from \emph{vastu}, \textquotedblleft{}a thing\textquotedblright{}, with the Malayalam locative ending -\ml{ത്തിൽ}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vāstavattil}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vāstavattil}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vāstavattil avaḷkkŭ ā jōli iṣṭamāyirunnilla.} — In reality she did not like that job.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for because of, then the Malayalam for actually, then say \emph{vāstavattil} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
